result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers advise against on-brand status colors, explain the brand-red/failure conflict, and require icons and labels. A goes further with specific hex pairs for all four statuses, a failure crimson kept apart from #d93a35, and contrast estimates it labels as estimates. B gives only hues, offers hex values later, and is somewhat vaguer on readability, though it does add the option of a non-red primary button and cites WCAG thresholds. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend keeping the usual status meanings and point out that a brand-red primary button would clash with a red failure state. B gives exact fill and text hex values for all four statuses, with icons, labels and contrast notes, while A names only hues and offers the hex values as a follow-up. B is slightly weaker on separating the brand red from failure, since it never suggests a non-red primary button, and its contrast ratios are labeled as estimates rather than measured.
